transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for fitting me in. Um... I guess the main reason I’m here is that I've been having a little trouble at work. I'm a registered nurse, and lately I just... I lose my train of thought on the floor a lot. 

It's probably just because hospitals are so chaotic, but, um... like, if an IV pump beeps, or someone asks another nurse a question nearby, or a call light goes off, suddenly I’ve just completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was working on. I mean, I know everyone gets distracted sometimes, right? I just really want to make sure I'm doing a good job for my patients, so... I was hoping you could tell me if that sounds normal, or if it's something I should be worried about?
How long have you been experiencing these episodes of losing your train of thought?

Well, um... I guess it's been happening for a while, but it really became, you know, a lot more noticeable—maybe a major problem—since I took on some expanded charge-nurse responsibilities. That was almost two years ago. 

I mean, before that, I could usually just power through it, you know? But with the extra duties, it's just... harder to keep everything straight. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline, is that the kind of information you need?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since you started having these episodes of losing your train of thought?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, I get a little frustrated with myself sometimes when I drop the ball on something, just because I really want to be a good nurse. But I wouldn't say I feel sad or down at all. 

I'm actually a pretty positive person most of the time! I always try to keep a smile on for my patients, you know? So, yeah, my mood has been totally fine. Is that... is that helpful to know? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?

Um, no, I wouldn't say so. I mean, the hospital can be a little stressful sometimes, just because it's so busy, but I don't really feel anxious or on edge at all. 

I actually feel pretty calm most of the time! It's just... you know, the getting distracted part that's the issue. But emotionally, I feel totally fine. Is it okay that I don't feel anxious? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of everything.
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened recently?

Oh, um, no, not really. My memory is actually pretty good! I don't have any trouble remembering what happened yesterday or, you know, earlier in the week. 

It's really just the... the in-the-moment stuff, like losing my train of thought right in the middle of doing something. But once something has happened, I remember it just fine. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound like my memory is failing or anything, because it's really not. Does that make sense?
Do you have trouble focusing on tasks?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say I have *trouble* focusing, exactly. I mean, I can definitely focus when I really need to! Like when I'm with a patient and they really need my attention, I'm totally there. 

It's just that sometimes, um, my mind might wander a little bit if I'm doing something repetitive, like charting or organizing supplies. But I always get it done eventually! I just might take a few extra breaks or... or get sidetracked for a minute. Is that normal? I mean, everyone's mind wanders a little bit, right? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound worse than it is, because I really do try my best to stay on task.
Do you have trouble paying attention to multiple things at the same time?

Um, actually, no, I don't think so. Multitasking is kind of a huge part of being a nurse, so I'm pretty used to it! I mean, you're always juggling a few things at once on the floor, like... like keeping an eye on an IV pump while listening to a patient's family, and I feel like I handle that part pretty well. 

I really try my best to keep all the plates spinning, you know? I wouldn't say I struggle with paying attention to a few things at once. I mean, everyone gets a little overwhelmed if it's *too* many things, right? But generally, I think I do okay with it. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you ever feel like you're in a fog or daze, like your thinking is cloudy or unclear?

Um, no, I really don't think so. I mean, sure, after a really long twelve-hour shift on the floor, I get a little physically exhausted, like anyone would, but I wouldn't ever call it a fog or a daze. My thinking is actually pretty clear! 

I try really hard to stay sharp, you know, especially because my patients rely on me so much. So, no, not cloudy at all. Well, maybe just before my first cup of coffee in the morning, but... but that's totally normal, right? I really hope I'm answering these the right way for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know. Is this the kind of information you're looking for?
Do you ever feel mentally confused or disorganized, even if it's just for a brief moment?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely wouldn't say I get confused! As a nurse, you really can't afford to be disorganized, so I make sure I stay on top of things. I have my little systems, you know? Like my report sheets and my checklists, so everything stays totally in order. 

I mean, I guess everyone has a split second where they walk into a supply room and forget what they went in for, right? That's just being human, especially when it's busy! But I always figure it out right away. I wouldn't call it being mentally disorganized at all. I really try to keep things running smoothly. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not overcomplicating my answers for you!
Do you have trouble maintaining attention when performing a task that requires sustained mental effort?

Um, well, I guess... maybe a little? But I really try not to let it affect my work! I mean, I love being at the bedside with my patients, so I always prioritize that. 

But, um, sometimes if I know a task is going to take a lot of, like, really focused chart review... like if I have to audit documentation across a few different shifts... I might, um, I might keep pushing it off? I just end up finding more bedside tasks to do instead, because sitting down and just staring at the screen for that long feels... I don't know, almost like trying to climb a wall? 

But I always get it done eventually! I just prefer being active on the floor, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad nurse. A lot of people prefer the hands-on stuff over the paperwork, right? Is that the kind of thing you meant?
Do you have trouble making decisions, even about small things?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble making decisions. I mean, as a nurse, you have to make a hundred little decisions every hour, right? And I do that just fine! I'm always able to decide what my patients need. 

I guess... well, maybe when it comes to really silly, personal things? Like if someone asks me where I want to go for dinner, I might just say, "Oh, wherever you want is fine!" But that's just because I want to be easygoing, you know? I don't want to be difficult or make a fuss over something so small. It's not that I *can't* decide, I just... I'd rather make the other person happy. That's a good thing, right? Being flexible? I just want to make sure I'm answering this the way you need me to.
Do you have trouble paying attention to several things at once when you're performing tasks?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, multitasking is basically the whole job description for a nurse, right? You're constantly juggling medications, call lights, charting, and talking to doctors. I'm used to it! 

I really try my best to keep all the plates spinning, and I think I do a pretty good job. I mean, I guess sometimes if a doctor is giving me a really complicated verbal order while an alarm is going off and a family member is trying to ask me a question, I might need to ask someone to repeat themselves? But I feel like anyone would get a little overwhelmed in that situation, wouldn't they? It's just a lot of noise. But I always make sure I get the information right, even if I have to double-check. I'm very careful about patient safety. That's just a normal part of working in a hospital, don't you think? I hope I'm explaining that okay!
Do you find that you're often distracted by things around you, like noises or conversations, when you're trying to focus on a task?

Um, well... I mean, hospitals are just naturally chaotic, right? There's always so much going on. So I think it's completely normal to notice things around you! I try really hard to stay focused on my patients, I really do. 

But I guess... well, to be completely honest, it is kind of the main reason I decided to come see you. I just... I feel like I'm losing my train of thought on the floor a lot lately? Like, I'll be trying to figure out a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps down the hall, or I hear someone asking another nurse a question, or a call light goes off... and it's like my brain just resets. Suddenly I've completely forgotten what I was just working on. 

I always figure it out eventually! I just have to retrace my steps. But it happens constantly, and I feel so terrible about it. I really don't want it to look like I'm not paying attention to my job, because I care so much about my patients. It's just hard to filter out all the extra noise sometimes. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent... I really am trying my best out there.
Do you find that your mind often wanders to thoughts unrelated to the task at hand when you're trying to focus?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I think my mind stays pretty much on track! When you're a nurse, you have to be so present for your patients, you know? I really pride myself on being there for them and listening to what they need. 

I guess... well, everybody daydreams a little bit, right? Like if I'm doing something super repetitive, like stocking the supply closet or something, maybe I'll start thinking about my grocery list or what I need to do after my shift. But that's just normal, isn't it? Everybody does that when they're doing chores! It's not like I'm zoning out when I'm doing something important, like drawing up meds. I'm always very careful then. I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answer. Is that what you mean by mind wandering? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm not focused on my work, because I really am.
Do you find it hard to ignore irrelevant sounds or conversations when you're trying to focus on something?

Oh, um... I feel like that's kind of what I was just mentioning a second ago? With the IV pumps and the other nurses talking? I'm so sorry, did I not explain that very well the first time? I can try to be more specific if you need me to! 

But, um, if you mean outside of the hospital... no, I don't think so. My house is usually pretty quiet, so I don't really have to worry about tuning things out when I'm at home. It's really just at work where the background noise seems to catch my attention so much. I just... I hope I'm answering what you're actually asking. Is that what you meant, or were you looking for a different kind of example? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find it difficult to refocus your attention after being distracted by something?

Um, no, I wouldn't say it's difficult! I mean, I always get back to what I was doing eventually. It might just take me a second to remember where I left off, but I always figure it out. 

Like I said before, I just have to retrace my steps a little bit. I think that's pretty normal when you get interrupted, right? Everyone needs a moment to gather their thoughts. I definitely don't just abandon my tasks or anything like that. I always make sure my patients are taken care of and my charting is done, even if it takes me a little longer because of all the interruptions. 

I just... I want to make sure you know I'm a hard worker. I don't just give up when I get distracted. I really push myself to get back on track. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.
Do you feel like your mind gets tired more easily than it used to, even after getting enough rest?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think my mind gets tired any faster than anyone else's! Nursing is just a really exhausting job, you know? Twelve-hour shifts take a lot out of you, both physically and mentally. 

Even if I sleep well on my days off, it's just... it's a lot of responsibility to carry around. So if I feel a little mentally drained sometimes, I think that's just the nature of the work, isn't it? It's not like my brain is broken or anything. I can still push through and do what I need to do. I always make sure I'm sharp for my patients. 

I just... I hope I don't sound like I'm complaining about my job, because I really do love it. I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right. Is it normal to feel a little mentally tired when you have a demanding career like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are for me.
Do you find it hard to concentrate when there are multiple things happening around you?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, the hospital is always chaotic, but I feel like I handle it pretty well! There's always a lot going on—doctors rounding, alarms going off, families asking questions—but I just kind of power through it, you know? 

I really try to stay on top of everything. If I'm doing a dressing change and someone calls my name, I just tell them I'll be right there and keep focusing on what I'm doing. I think I'm pretty good at juggling things. I mean, you have to be in this job, right? 

I definitely don't let the chaos stop me from doing my job properly. I always make sure I'm giving my full attention to whoever I'm with at that moment. I just... I really hope that doesn't make me sound scattered. I'm actually very organized! I just want to make sure I'm answering this the right way. Does that sound like a normal response for someone in my field?
Do you find it harder to concentrate when you're trying to learn new information or perform a task that requires a lot of mental effort?

Um, well, I wouldn't say it's *hard* to concentrate, exactly. I mean, I can definitely learn new things! I just finished a module on new IV pumps last month and did fine. 

But, um... I guess if it's something that requires a lot of, like, sitting down and really digging through paperwork... I might put it off a little bit? Like, sometimes we have to do these deep-dive chart audits, looking at documentation across multiple shifts. And, um, if I know I have to do that, I'll usually try to find other things to do first. Like, I'll go check on my patients again, or restock the supply cart, or help another nurse with a turn. 

It's not that I *can't* do the audits! I always get them done before the deadline. It's just that sitting down to start them feels a little bit like... I don't know, trying to climb a wall? It just takes a lot of mental energy to get going on it. But I think that's just because I'm such a hands-on, bedside kind of nurse, you know? I prefer being up and moving and helping people directly rather than staring at a screen. 

That's a good thing, right? To want to be at the bedside? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound like I'm avoiding my work, because I really do get it all done eventually. I hope that makes sense.
Do you find it difficult to screen out background noise or irrelevant conversations when you're trying to focus on a task?

Um... well, honestly, I guess that is kind of why I finally decided to come in. I mean, I really try my best to tune things out, but... the floor is just so loud, you know? 

It's not that I can't do my job! I really want to emphasize that. But... lately, I've noticed I lose my train of thought a lot. Like, constantly. I'll be right in the middle of figuring out a patient flow issue, or calculating a drip rate, and then... an IV pump beeps down the hall, or I hear someone asking another nurse a question, or a call light goes off. And it's like my brain just completely drops whatever I was doing. I suddenly have no idea what I was just thinking about. 

It's really embarrassing, honestly. I try to hide it so my coworkers don't think I'm incompetent or anything. I just... I really want to be a good nurse, and I feel like a good nurse shouldn't get so derailed by normal hospital noises. Is it... is it okay that I struggle with that? I mean, a lot of nurses probably get distracted by all the beeping, right? I just hope I'm not making myself sound like a liability or something. I really do care about my patients.
